subject: [PATCH v4 3/3] mm: zswap: drop cold writeback folios via swap dropbehind

reviews.author: Kunwu Chan
reviews.summary: Reviewer Kunwu Chan confirmed that the patch addresses their previous concern about a refcount overlap by dropping the zswap reference before __swap_writepage(), ensuring that remove_mapping_reclaim() sees the expected refcount.
reviews.raw_body:
Thanks for addressing this.

I checked the refcount handoff in v4. Dropping the zswap reference before 
__swap_writepage() removes the refcount overlap I was concerned about in v3. 
The swapcache reference keeps the folio alive until writeback starts, and 
folio_end_writeback() takes the completion reference before clearing 
PG_writeback, so remove_mapping_reclaim() sees the expected refcount.

Reviewed-by: Kunwu Chan <kunwu.chan@gmail.com>

Thanks, 
KunWu

2026-09-08.patch_summary: This patch optimizes the zswap writeback process by dropping cold folios from the swap cache after they are written back to disk, rather than leaving them on the LRU for reclaim. This is done by allocating the folio off the LRU and marking it PG_dropbehind, which allows the swap dropbehind path to free the folio once writeback completes. The patch aims to reduce memory residency time for cold pages and improve system performance.
